findings.evidence: Mathlib/Algebra/Polynomial/Smeval.lean:243 `smeval_mul_X : (p * X).smeval x = p.smeval x * x`, :257 `smeval_mul_X_pow : (p * X ^ n).smeval x = p.smeval x * x ^ n`, :266 `smeval_mul : (p * q).smeval x = ...`, :272 `smeval_pow`. `pow_mul_smeval` does not have the collision (its prefix is not `smeval_`), so only `smeval_mul_pow` is wrong on its own; the rename of the mirror is for consistency.
findings.fix: Rename to describe the whole equation, e.g. `smeval_mul_pow_eq_pow_mul_smeval`, and rename the mirror `pow_mul_smeval` (line 132) to match for symmetry; update the module-doc list at lines 31-32 and the uses at Semiconj.lean:157 and DividedPowers/Commutation.lean (via `ringChoose_mul_pow`).
findings.issue: `smeval_mul_pow` in namespace `TauCeti.Polynomial` states `smeval p a * x ^ n = x ^ n * smeval p (a + n • c)`, but in the `Polynomial` namespace the `smeval_<expr>` prefix uniformly names the *polynomial* being evaluated, so the name reads as `(p * q ^ n).smeval x`. The two families are visible together under `open Polynomial TauCeti.Polynomial`.

summary: Prior-round naming issues are fixed. One name remains misleading: `TauCeti.Polynomial.smeval_mul_pow` uses the `smeval_` prefix, which throughout Mathlib's `Polynomial` namespace means "smeval of this polynomial expression", to instead describe a product of an evaluation with a ring power.
